title: Thoughts from a first time Fable user
author: Lesleylizasaurus
selftext:
I had a full GDD going in- complete story written out, levels planned, puzzles worked out, a battle system, etc. I already had music I created as well. I did use GPT to create some placeholder assets.

Signed up for the base model of Fable, and spent another $100 on additional credits.

I tried using gamemaker but just couldn’t make it work for me, so I used Fable to start building my game as HTML5 for now. 

Animations aside (gotta figure those out), I’ve got a complete vertical slice of the first level of the game with all interactions etc. I also have the bones of the next two levels in place and the beginnings of the battle system. I’m sure I could be doing this more efficiently, but it’s so amazing seeing something I’ve been dreaming up in my head for a decade come to life.

I’ve got to slow down on my build because I don’t want to blow through money, but I figure I can work on better art and animations in my downtown between buying credits. 

I had no idea how fantastic fable would be but I absolutely recommend it for anyone who has a well thought out idea and needs some help bringing it to life!

comments.author: dblkil
comments.body:
Fable 5 is meh.

Burns through usage/tokens like nuts.

Opus is enough.

In most cases sonnet is probably enough.

You wouldn't be able to tell the difference much, unless you're a senior coder.

replies.author: DaedalusRaistlin
replies.body:
Yeah, I've gone back to using Sonnet to try to save some quota, and it's managing pretty well in my 50k player soccer game (three.js and WebGPU.)

I used Opus to write the initial swarm logic for a different game, because Fable was down. Got it working pretty quickly. 

I'm impressed by some of what Fable can do. But I don't think I'd put more money into it once it runs out. 
I'd probably instead get Fable to write a detailed roadmap, and then use a lesser version to implement it.

It's easy to think the lesser models aren't capable. But you might be surprised at how well they can do. 

- Someone who's pro quota keeps running out very quickly

comments.author: superkickstart
comments.body: You dont need claude/fable for that. Also don't try to do too much at once. Things get expensive fast and the results arent usually the best. Split it to more manageable tasks and document everything while you do it (and let ai document what it's doing) so it can be referenced and used as context when you swap ai's around for different tasks. Keep things generic and don't build your processes around one provider. My monthly ai budget is less than 50 euros and I can pretty much develop anything I can imagine.

comments.author: patchfoot02
comments.body:
Its a waste of money to have fable do all that. Any model can make web games with code spaghetti under the hood and fable will just do the same thing for a way higher cost unless you give it specific boundaries on what kind of code to write. Where fable can have some advantage is in writing architecture and plans for actual durable code patterns which is the difficult part.   
  
The key is if you are telling fable/opus/gpt to just write code design plans then they don't sprint to task completion with wonky code that'll fall apart once you really get going. If the task is make a little guy run around the screen and stab orcs or whatever they don't stop and think about maintaining the code and adding features on the next turn. They have no state so nothing exists but the current turn and task. They blitz to task completion because that's what they are trained to do.   
  
You don't even need to understand software engineering just tell them to write up system design docs and decompose those into discrete implementation tasks. Its better if you know software engineering but if you don't just getting the models to stop and plan for a whole turn they can do alright. Then once its time to write the code that's something you can have nearly any decent model execute (even qwen locally if you have a decent enough gpu) if they've been given a good set of plans to follow.  
  
Frontier model plan, cheap model execute is the way to not burn money and make actual durable progress.

comments.author: MidSerpent
comments.body: Fable really favors big front loaded plans, so starting with a GDD like that is a big part of why you got such a good result.
